title: Extract phone_focus_mode with focus_policy into one public repo
objective: Move the GPS focus enforcer and its Python policy half out together, since focus_policy parses phone_focus_mode's config.sh and is referenced by nothing else. The repo is public and the subject matter is a home location, so proving no coordinate leaks is part of the job, not an afterthought.
acceptance_criteria: Both trees land in one public repo with full history and python_pkg.focus_policy imports rewritten.
The full git history contains no real home coordinate and no committed config_secrets.sh, verified BEFORE the repo is made public.
The new repo has a .gitignore covering config_secrets.sh; none came across in the filter-repo pass.
The Python suites pass from a clean clone: 161 tests.
The shell suites pass with NO config_secrets.sh present, which means the harness must pin its own coordinates instead of inheriting real ones.
config.sh can be sourced without a secrets file, so CI and a fresh clone work.
Any suite that does not pass is skipped in CI with a stated reason, and its behaviour is compared against the pre-extraction baseline to establish whether the split caused it.
The monorepo's remaining tests still pass and no config, hook or workflow names a removed path.
out_of_scope: hosts and digital_wellbeing, deferred while the guard-lib repoint is pending.
Fixing test_magisk_service.sh, which was already broken and is not a regression from this split.
python-tests.yml's stale lichess_bot and tests/ path filters, absent since May 2026.
verifier: git log --all -p greps clean for the home coordinates; pytest reports 161 passed in the new repo; the shell suites run with the secrets file moved away; pytest linux_configuration/tests reports 178 passed here; check_shell_coverage.sh --all and check_python_location.sh over every .py both exit 0; check_directory_depth.sh --all drops 262 -> 248.
